description.en: 1 January. At midnight the Packhorse Inn sings “Auld Lang Syne” with Mrs Birkett, and the first-footer brings coal, bread and salt.
description.sl: 1. januarja. Ob polnoči gospa Birkett in vsa gostilna Packhorse zapojejo »Auld Lang Syne«, prvi gost v novem letu pa prinese premog, kruh in sol.
description.it: 1º gennaio. A mezzanotte la signora Birkett e tutta la locanda Packhorse cantano «Auld Lang Syne», e il primo ospite dell'anno porta carbone, pane e sale.
description.de: 1. Januar. Um Mitternacht singen Frau Birkett und das ganze Packhorse Inn „Auld Lang Syne“, und der erste Gast des Jahres bringt Kohle, Brot und Salz.

words.example_en: At midnight everyone sings “Auld Lang Syne”.
words.example_it: A mezzanotte tutti cantano «Auld Lang Syne».
words.example_de: Um Mitternacht singen alle „Auld Lang Syne“.
words.note: at midnight, at night, but in the evening.
words.note_sl: at midnight (opolnoči), at night (ponoči), a in the evening (zvečer).
words.note_it: at midnight (a mezzanotte), at night (di notte), ma in the evening (di sera).
words.note_de: at midnight (um Mitternacht), at night (nachts), aber in the evening (abends).

words.example_en: The first-footer brings coal, bread and salt.
words.example_sl: Prvi gost v novem letu prinese premog, kruh in sol.
words.example_it: Il primo ospite dell'anno porta carbone, pane e sale.
words.example_de: Der erste Gast im neuen Jahr bringt Kohle, Brot und Salz.
words.note: A northern custom: the first visitor after midnight brings luck. A tall, dark man brings the most.
words.note_sl: Običaj na severu: prvi obiskovalec po polnoči prinese srečo. Največ sreče prinese visok, temnolas moški.
words.note_it: Un'usanza del Nord: il primo visitatore dopo mezzanotte porta fortuna. Ne porta di più un uomo alto e moro.
words.note_de: Ein Brauch im Norden: Der erste Besucher nach Mitternacht bringt Glück. Am meisten bringt ein großer, dunkelhaariger Mann.

words.example_en: Coal keeps the house warm all year.
words.example_it: Il carbone tiene calda la casa tutto l'anno.
words.example_de: Kohle hält das Haus das ganze Jahr warm.
words.note: Uncountable: some coal, a piece of coal.
words.note_sl: Neštevno: some coal, a piece of coal (kos premoga).
words.note_it: Non numerabile: some coal, a piece of coal (un pezzo di carbone).
words.note_de: Nicht zählbar: some coal, a piece of coal (ein Stück Kohle).

words.example_en: Bread and salt mean there's always food on the table.
words.example_sl: Kruh in sol pomenita, da je na mizi vedno hrana.
words.example_it: Pane e sale vogliono dire che in tavola c'è sempre da mangiare.
words.example_de: Brot und Salz bedeuten, dass immer Essen auf dem Tisch steht.

words.example_en: Ten, nine, eight … It's the countdown to midnight!
words.example_sl: Deset, devet, osem … Odštevanje do polnoči!
words.example_it: Dieci, nove, otto… È il conto alla rovescia fino a mezzanotte!
words.example_de: Zehn, neun, acht … Der Countdown bis Mitternacht!

words.example_en: My New Year's resolution: I'm going to learn ten words every day.
words.example_sl: Moja novoletna zaobljuba: vsak dan se bom naučil deset besed.
words.example_it: Il mio buon proposito per l'anno nuovo: imparerò dieci parole al giorno.
words.example_de: Mein guter Vorsatz fürs neue Jahr: Ich lerne jeden Tag zehn Wörter.
words.note: A New Year's resolution is a promise to yourself for the new year.
words.note_sl: New Year's resolution je obljuba samemu sebi za novo leto.
words.note_it: Una New Year's resolution è una promessa a sé stessi per l'anno nuovo.
words.note_de: Eine New Year's resolution ist ein Versprechen an sich selbst fürs neue Jahr.

words.example_en: The grown-ups say “Cheers!”, and the children drink lemonade.
words.example_sl: Odrasli rečejo »Na zdravje!«, otroci pa pijejo limonado.
words.example_it: I grandi dicono «Salute!», e i bambini bevono la limonata.
words.example_de: Die Großen sagen „Prost!“, und die Kinder trinken Limonade.
words.note_it: In Gran Bretagna «Cheers!» vuol dire anche «Grazie!» e «Ciao!».
